sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半打电话给总统，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中度过的七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能几乎每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个平底锅就能做完的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受优惠，网址为nytimes.com斜杠subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Yesterday on the show, we went inside Donald Trump's campaign for president to understand how he's trying to turn a mountain of legal trouble into a political advantage.
sentences.zh: 昨天的节目中，我们深入探讨了唐纳德·特朗普的总统竞选活动，以了解他如何试图将堆积如山的法律麻烦转化为政治优势。

sentences.en: Today, we turn to the re-election campaign of President Biden.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们转向拜登总统的连任竞选。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Reed Epstein, about why what looks like a record of accomplishment on paper is turning out to be so difficult to campaign on.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事里德·爱泼斯坦进行了交谈，探讨为什么纸面上看似亮眼的政绩在竞选中却如此难以施展。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月3日，星期三。

sentences.en: Reed, hi.
sentences.zh: 里德，你好。

sentences.en: Sabrina, hi.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，你好。

sentences.en: So, Reed, yesterday our esteemed colleague, Maggie Haberman, was on the show, and she was talking about Donald Trump's 2024 campaign strategy.
sentences.zh: 那么，里德，昨天我们尊敬的同事玛吉·哈伯曼上了节目，她谈到了唐纳德·特朗普2024年的竞选策略。

sentences.en: And, fittingly, we come to you to talk about what Joe Biden's 2024 strategy will be like.
sentences.zh: 顺理成章地，我们来找你聊聊乔·拜登2024年的策略会是怎样的。

sentences.en: Biden, of course, has presided over a relatively strong economy.
sentences.zh: 当然，拜登执政期间的经济表现相对强劲。

sentences.en: He's passed a bunch of legislation, some of it very sweeping, some of it even bipartisan, despite historic levels of partisanship.
sentences.zh: 他通过了一系列立法，其中有些影响深远，甚至在极端的两极分化背景下得到了两党支持。

sentences.en: And the presumptive nominee on the other side is facing 91 felony counts.
sentences.zh: 而另一边的假定提名人正面临91项重罪指控。

sentences.en: And yet, and I know it's early, but I have to be honest, so far it's been a little hard to figure out what Biden's message actually is.
sentences.zh: 然而——我知道现在还早，但我必须说实话——到目前为止，人们还是有点难以弄清拜登的信息到底是什么。

sentences.en: So, Reed, what is Biden running on?
sentences.zh: 那么，里德，拜登的竞选纲领是什么？

sentences.en: Well, part of Biden's problem is that a lot of these things that you articulated that should be strengths for him, frankly, are not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，拜登的问题之一在于，你刚才提到的很多本该成为他优势的方面，坦白说，并没有起到这个作用。

sentences.en: They're political weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 它们成了政治软肋。

sentences.en: He's been trying to sell his record and trying to explain to people that their lives are better under him.
sentences.zh: 他一直在试图兜售自己的政绩，并试图向人们解释，在领导下他们的生活更好了。

sentences.en: But the thing that you're seeing is that a lot of these things that Biden accomplished, he's not able to talk about because voters don't think that they're selling points.
sentences.zh: 但你看到的情况是，拜登取得的许多成就，他根本无法宣扬，因为选民并不认为这些是卖点。

sentences.en: Can you give me an example?
sentences.zh: 你能举个例子吗？

sentences.en: Well, the economy is really the biggest one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，经济绝对是最大的一项。

sentences.en: All of the indicators that we have on the economy would tell you that the economy is booming, that things are going great.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握的所有经济指标都表明经济正在蓬勃发展，一切都在向好。

sentences.en: But if you ask people about how they feel about the economy, they don't feel good about it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你问人们对经济的感受，他们并不觉得好。

sentences.en: People see that prices are still up.
sentences.zh: 人们看到物价依然居高不下。

sentences.en: They see that they can't buy a house because the interest rates are high.
sentences.zh: 他们看到因为利率高而买不起房。

sentences.en: And so none of that is great for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以这些对乔·拜登来说都不是什么好事。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is determined to reward hard work.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登决心回报辛勤的工作。

sentences.en: They spent about $40 million in battleground states.
sentences.zh: 他们在摇摆州花费了约4000万美元。

sentences.en: Over 12 million jobs have been created.
sentences.zh: 创造了超过1200万个就业岗位。

sentences.en: Trying to sell the president's economic record.
sentences.zh: 试图宣传总统的经济政绩。

sentences.en: Bidenomics.
sentences.zh: 拜登经济学。

sentences.en: Bidenomics.
sentences.zh: 拜登经济学。

sentences.en: We're investing in places and people that have been forgotten.
sentences.zh: 我们正在投资那些被遗忘的地方和人们。

sentences.en: And the net effect of that so far has not been any great change in the polls.
sentences.zh: 而到目前为止，这带来的整体效果并没有让民调发生任何巨大的改变。

sentences.en: In fact, the polls for Joe Biden have gotten worse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，乔·拜登的民调数据反而变得更糟了。

sentences.en: And it seems pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 而且情况似乎很明朗。

sentences.en: I'm Joe Biden, and I approve this message.
sentences.zh: 我是乔·拜登，我批准了这条信息。

sentences.en: The advertising that they've done has not really worked.
sentences.zh: 他们制作的广告并没有真正起作用。

sentences.en: So basically, bottom line, the economy, despite all of the economists telling us it should add up to a strength for Joe Biden in his campaign, has not.
sentences.zh: 所以总而言之，尽管所有经济学家都告诉我们经济本该成为乔·拜登竞选的强项，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What are the other accomplishments, aside from the economy, that he could be running on that would potentially be a strength?
sentences.zh: 除了经济之外，他还能以哪些其他的成就作为可能成为优势的竞选筹码呢？

sentences.en: Well, he did pass a bunch of pretty significant pieces of legislation on infrastructure, on climate investments, on the CHIPS Act.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他确实通过了一系列相当重要的立法，涉及基础设施、气候投资以及《芯片法案》。

sentences.en: All of these laws are spending exorbitant amounts of money all around the country for projects that will build new bridges, that will build solar factories.
sentences.zh: 所有这些法律都在全国各地投入了巨额资金，用于建造新桥梁、建设太阳能工厂等项目。

sentences.en: All things that pull very well individually.
sentences.zh: 单拿出来看，这些都是极受民意欢迎的事情。

sentences.en: People say that they want, but you can't snap your fingers and have a new bridge.
sentences.zh: 人们说他们想要这些，但你不可能打个响指就凭空变出一座新桥。

sentences.en: Some of these things take years and years to happen.
sentences.zh: 其中一些项目需要数年时间才能实现。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, what people see on infrastructure, frankly, is road construction.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，坦白说，人们在基础设施方面看到的就是道路施工。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in a lot of these states, you have local officials that are taking credit for projects that federal legislation is subsidizing that Joe Biden signed.
sentences.zh: 在许多这样的州，地方官员正在将联邦立法资助且由乔·拜登签署的项目归功于自己。

sentences.en: And so a lot of federal money has flowed to Georgia, and you have the Republican governor, Brian Kemp, who's running around taking credit for it.
sentences.zh: 因此，大量联邦资金流入了佐治亚州，而共和党州长布赖恩·坎普却到处把功劳揽到自己身上。

sentences.en: There's a bridge between Cincinnati and Kentucky that the governor of Kentucky and Mitch McConnell have taken a lot of credit for.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提和肯塔基州之间有一座桥，肯塔基州州长和米奇·麦康奈尔就把它的大部分功劳揽了过去。

sentences.en: And so not only are these projects not immediate, people don't see immediate results on it, but he's competing with local officials to take credit for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些项目不仅不具有即时性，人们看不到立竿见影的效果，而且他还在跟地方官员争抢功劳。

sentences.en: Reed, you mentioned big legislation, and I know that part of what passed in the legislation that our colleagues were writing about a lot last year, the Inflation Reduction Act,
sentences.zh: 里德，你提到了重大立法，我知道去年我们的同事大量报道的立法中有一部分是《通胀削减法案》，

sentences.en: had to do with climate and climate change and kind of alleviating some of the effects of it.
sentences.zh: 这与气候、气候变化以及某种程度上缓解其影响有关。

sentences.en: I would imagine that would play pretty well with his base.
sentences.zh: 我想这在很大程度上会迎合他的核心选民。

sentences.en: Can he campaign on that?
sentences.zh: 他能用这个来进行竞选吗？

sentences.en: He has campaigned on that.
sentences.zh: 他确实以此进行过竞选。

sentences.en: I traveled with him this summer to a factory in Milwaukee that was making charging stations for electric vehicles.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天我跟他一起去过密尔沃基的一家工厂，那里正在制造电动汽车充电桩。

sentences.en: But again, a lot of these projects are just getting off the ground.
sentences.zh: 但同样，许多项目才刚刚起步。

sentences.en: It's going to take a while for those things to have an impact on people's lived experiences.
sentences.zh: 这些事情要对人们的生活经验产生影响还需要一段时间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK, so, Reed, you're saying essentially that the typical strategy of an incumbent president, you know, where you point to the things you've accomplished over your time in office,
sentences.zh: 好吧，里德，你的意思是，现任总统的典型策略——你知道，就是列举你在任期间取得的成就——

sentences.en: is not exactly working for Biden for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于各种原因，对拜登来说并不是很奏效。

sentences.en: But what about pointing to the thing that Biden would argue his presidency kind of represents?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果转而强调拜登认为他的总统任期所代表的东西呢？

sentences.en: You know, the sort of larger idea of democracy, upholding democratic norms and protecting them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如关于民主的宏大理念，维护和保护民主规范。

sentences.en: That seems like a clear way to draw a contrast between himself and former President Trump that would be something his campaign would latch on to.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个将自己与前总统特朗普区分开来的清晰方式，也是他的竞选团队会抓住不放的重点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, if you remember when he ran in 2020, he talked about restoring the soul of America and that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你还记得他在2020年参选时，他谈到了重塑美国的灵魂，而且你知道，

sentences.en: after January 6th became imbued with the idea of protecting democracy.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日事件之后，这被注入了保护民主的理念。

sentences.en: But there wasn't anything really for Biden to do on that front other than talk about it.
sentences.zh: 但除了谈论之外，拜登在这一方面实际上并没有什么可做的。

sentences.en: So even though the president has talked about democracy and talked about himself as the person upholding it,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管总统一直在谈论民主，并把自己塑造成捍卫民主的人，

sentences.en: we haven't seen that voters are racing to back him because of that issue.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有看到选民因为这个议题而争先恐后地支持他。

sentences.en: And Reed, what does the polling say?
sentences.zh: 那么里德，民调是怎么说的？

sentences.en: The polling says that people who are interested in democracy as an issue, they're interested in other issues more usually.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，那些将民主视为议题的人，通常对其他议题更感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think it's instructive to look at the midterm elections in Wisconsin, how Democrats attacked this issue when they were running against Ron Johnson,
sentences.zh: 我认为看看威斯康星州的中期选举很有启发意义，民主党人在对抗罗恩·约翰逊时是如何攻击这个议题的，

sentences.en: who was a senator who has been kind of a font of misinformation, who sort of questioned the results of the election, cast doubts on what happened on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·约翰逊是一位参议员，他某种程度上可以说是虚假信息的源头，他曾质疑选举结果，并对1月6日发生的事情表示怀疑。

sentences.en: You know, they did not run against him as an election denier or someone who was amplifying misinformation because every which way they tested it in polls and focus groups.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在竞选中并没有把他当作一个“选举否定论者”或放大虚假信息的人来攻击，因为无论他们在民调和焦点小组中以何种方式测试这一点，

sentences.en: They found that the most effective way of getting people to not vote for him was to talk about his economic record and not about his stance on democracy or misinformation.
sentences.zh: 他们都发现，让人不投票给他的最有效方法是谈论他的经济政绩，而不是他关于民主或虚假信息的立场。

sentences.en: And they ultimately, like, Ron Johnson won.
sentences.zh: 而且最终，罗恩·约翰逊赢了。

sentences.en: And so they can have a debate about whether the strategy was right or not.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以就这种策略是否正确展开辩论。

sentences.en: But they had spent a lot of time and had a vested interest in defeating him and concluded that democracy was not the best way to do it.
sentences.zh: 但他们曾花费大量时间并投入了巨大心血去击败他，并得出结论认为，民主并不是实现这一目标的最佳途径。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真是有趣。

sentences.en: That democracy, I guess, is just this abstract thing that doesn't necessarily on its own as a word mean much to people.
sentences.zh: 我猜民主只是一个抽象的概念，单凭这个词本身，对人们来说并不一定有多大意义。

sentences.en: Well, and what they found in Wisconsin was that any voter who cared about democracy as an issue was already going to vote for the Democratic candidates.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在威斯康星州发现的是，任何关心民主议题的选民无论如何都已经会投票给民主党候选人了。

sentences.en: OK, so democracy, not really a thing for swing voters, not an arrow he can put in his quiver.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以民主并不是摇摆选民关注的事，也不是他箭袋里的一支可用之箭。

sentences.en: What about the fact that Trump is facing multiple indictments?
sentences.zh: 那特朗普面临多项起诉这件事呢？

sentences.en: I mean, come March, he's scheduled to be on trial in federal court, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，到了三月份，他预定要在联邦法院受审，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, is that a strength for Biden?
sentences.zh: 这算不算是拜登的优势？

sentences.en: I mean, something he'd want to sell on the campaign trail?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是他想在竞选之路上大肆宣传的东西吗？

sentences.en: This is sort of the trickiest issue for Joe Biden as he's running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 这是乔·拜登竞选连任时遇到的最棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Joe Biden has said from the beginning that he will not interfere or discuss Donald Trump's legal issues because he ran for president on the idea of restoring the independence of the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登从一开始就表示，他不会干涉或讨论唐纳德·特朗普的法律问题，因为他竞选总统的理念就是恢复司法部的独立性。

sentences.en: And he does not want to back off of that in any way.
sentences.zh: 他绝不想在这一点上有任何退缩。

sentences.en: Despite what Trump says on a daily basis where he is blaming Biden for the prosecution of him,
sentences.zh: 尽管特朗普每天都在指责拜登是针对他的起诉的幕后黑手，

sentences.en: Biden does not want to give that any credence.
sentences.zh: 拜登并不想给这种说法赋予任何可信度。

sentences.en: So he doesn't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以他不谈论此事。

sentences.en: He has instructed his campaign not to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他指示他的竞选团队不要谈论此事。

sentences.en: He's instructed the Democratic National Committee not to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他指示民主党全国委员会不要谈论此事。

sentences.en: And so the biggest organizations that are devoted to re-electing Joe Biden president and his White House have taken a collective vow of silence
sentences.zh: 因此，那些致力于让乔·拜登连任总统以及白宫的最大组织，集体发誓保持沉默，

sentences.en: on the biggest thing concerning Donald Trump in the next year.
sentences.zh: 对明年涉及唐纳德·特朗普的最大事情闭口不言。

sentences.en: In other words, he doesn't want to be seen as having put his thumb on the scale with his Justice Department in these federal prosecutions of Trump.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他不想让人觉得他在联邦对特朗普的起诉中通过司法部暗中施加了影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK, so you've laid out this list of would-be strengths that are functioning really at this point as weaknesses for Biden,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你已经列出了一系列本该是优势、但现在对拜登来说实际上却成了劣势的事情，

sentences.en: you know, things he wants to talk about but really can't, which leads me to wonder if his strengths are this weak.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些他想谈却又实在不能谈的事情，这不禁让我纳闷，如果他的优势这么弱，

sentences.en: What about his actual weaknesses?
sentences.zh: 那他真正的劣势呢？

sentences.en: Tell me about those.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊这些吧。

sentences.en: Well, if you ask voters about it, and we've done polls, I've gone door to door with candidates, and you ask people, what do you think of Joe Biden?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你去问选民，我们做过民调，我也曾和候选人挨家挨户拜访选民，当你问大家“你怎么看乔·拜登”时，

sentences.en: Inevitably, the first response is, I can't believe he's so old.
sentences.zh: 不可避免的第一反应总是：“我真不敢相信他这么老了。”

sentences.en: Every poll has suggested that it's a big problem.
sentences.zh: 每一项民调都表明这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: And it's the one thing that they can't change.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们无法改变的一点。

sentences.en: In theory, they could fix their economic messaging.
sentences.zh: 理论上，他们可以修复经济传达的信息。

sentences.en: The economy could get better.
sentences.zh: 经济可能会好转。

sentences.en: But there's nothing they can do about Joe Biden being 81 years old.
sentences.zh: 但对于乔·拜登已经81岁这件事，他们什么也做不了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the way that people view him, certainly the Trump campaign and Republicans will do everything they can to take advantage of,
sentences.zh: 人们对他的看法，当然特朗普的竞选团队和共和党人会竭尽全力去加以利用，

sentences.en: you know, when he tripped during a graduation ceremony or fell on the stairs going up to Air Force One.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如他在毕业典礼上绊倒，或者在登上空军一号的阶梯时摔倒。

sentences.en: I know that people who work for Biden live in fear of that happening on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 我知道为拜登工作的人经常生活在担心这种事发生的恐惧之中。

sentences.en: So what's his campaign doing to combat this age problem he has?
sentences.zh: 那么他的竞选团队在采取什么措施来应对他面临的年龄问题呢？

sentences.en: I know I'm 198 years old.
sentences.zh: 我知道我已经198岁了。

sentences.en: Well, he has started to make some jokes about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他开始拿这开玩笑了。

sentences.en: I know I don't look that old.
sentences.zh: 我知道我看起来没那么老。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I'm a little under 103.
sentences.zh: 我才不到103岁。

sentences.en: Well, I believe in the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我相信宪法第一修正案。

sentences.en: Not just because my good friend Jimmy Madison wrote it.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为我的好朋友吉米·麦迪逊写了它。

sentences.en: He has made jokes about being around with the founding fathers.
sentences.zh: 他开过自己和国父们一起经历过时代的玩笑。

sentences.en: But he hasn't, like, fully leaned into the age question in a way that that experience is what the country needs,
sentences.zh: 但他并没有完全顺应年龄的问题来阐述这种经验正是国家所需的，

sentences.en: which frankly leaves him vulnerable when he does have senior moments.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这让他在出现老年人那种糊涂时刻时显得十分脆弱。

sentences.en: You know, everybody has dealt with aging relatives, grandparents, parents, and seen how people slow down when they get older.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每个人都应对过年迈的亲戚、祖父母、父母，也见证过人们随着年纪增长而反应迟钝。

sentences.en: And the real danger is that people start to see that in him and wonder whether he's up for the job.
sentences.zh: 真正的危险在于，人们开始在他身上看到这一点，并怀疑他是否还能胜任这份工作。

sentences.en: So what are they doing instead then?
sentences.zh: 那他们转而采取什么措施呢？

sentences.en: Like, what's the strategy?
sentences.zh: 比如，策略是什么？

sentences.en: Just not have him out there so he won't potentially trip?
sentences.zh: 干脆不让他公开露面，免得他可能绊倒？

sentences.en: Like, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, he doesn't do as many events, certainly as Barack Obama did when he was running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他出席的公开活动确实没有那么多，肯定比贝拉克·奥巴马竞选连任时要少。

sentences.en: His days are shorter than other presidents.
sentences.zh: 他的工作时间比其他总统要短。

sentences.en: He doesn't do a lot of one-on-one interviews with sort of mainstream straight news reporters.
sentences.zh: 他不经常接受主流传统新闻记者的专访。

sentences.en: Instead, they have tried to sort of package him in a way online and have people vouch for him in the press.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们试图在网络上包装他，并让其他人通过媒体为他做担保。

sentences.en: I'm here to tell the truth about the Biden-Harris record and also...
sentences.zh: 我来这里是为了讲述拜登-哈里斯执政记录的真相，还有……

sentences.en: Gavin Newsom, the governor of California, did a debate against Ron DeSantis on Fox News where Newsom spent much of the debate defending the Biden record.
sentences.zh: 加州州长加文·纽森在福克斯新闻网与罗恩·德桑蒂斯进行了一场辩论，纽森在辩论中花了很多时间为拜登的执政记录辩护。

sentences.en: Biden administration, the last three years, has been a massive...
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在过去的三年里，一直在进行大规模的……

sentences.en: Joe Biden paying you tonight is...
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登今晚给你的报酬是……

sentences.en: 3.9 percent...
sentences.zh: 百分之三点九……

sentences.en: I thought this was state versus state.
sentences.zh: 我以为这是各州之间的较量。

sentences.en: But it's about the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 但这是关于美利坚合众国的。

sentences.en: I thought this guy was running for president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我还以为这家伙是在竞选美国总统呢。

sentences.en: It almost sounded like he thought that it was on the rest of the party to pull Joe Biden over the line as opposed to Biden doing it himself.
sentences.zh: 听起来他好像认为，拉乔·拜登一把主要是其他党内同仁的责任，而不是拜登自己的事。

sentences.en: And usually in a presidential election, it is on the candidate to do that, not necessarily on his surrogates.
sentences.zh: 通常在总统大选中，这是候选人自己的责任，不一定非得靠他的代理人。

sentences.en: But because of Joe Biden's age, because his own popularity is so low and the popularity of many of his surrogates are so high,
sentences.zh: 但由于乔·拜登的年龄问题，由于他自己的支持率如此之低，而他的许多代理人的支持率又如此之高，

sentences.en: Newsom and others have come to the conclusion that they have to be the ones to convince voters to vote for Joe Biden almost more than Joe Biden doing it.
sentences.zh: 纽森和其他人得出的结论是，他们必须成为说服选民投票给乔·拜登的人，这甚至比乔·拜登本人去争取还要重要。

sentences.en: So Reid, taking all of this together, what kind of path does that leave Biden in his campaign?
sentences.zh: 那么，里德，综合这一切来看，这给拜登的竞选之路留下了什么样的空间？

sentences.en: Well, Joe Biden, as we talked about, is not very popular.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们所讨论的，乔·拜登并不是很受欢迎。

sentences.en: Voters think he's very old.
sentences.zh: 选民们认为他太老了。

sentences.en: But the upside for him is that he appears to have the good fortune of running against Donald Trump, who's even less popular than he is.
sentences.zh: 但对他来说积极的一面是，他似乎运气很好，他的竞选对手唐纳德·特朗普比他更不受欢迎。

sentences.en: You know, in politics, like in everything else, you have to play to your strengths.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在政治中，就像在其他事情一样，你必须发挥自己的优势。

sentences.en: And it's left him to try to make the case to voters that he's better than Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这使得他不得不向选民力证自己比唐纳德·特朗普更好。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》这款游戏，这是《纽约时报》解谜游戏之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天都制作“拼字蜜蜂”和“连字盘”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那几位一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 从今天开始游戏。

sentences.en: So, Reid, you just explained to me all of the things Biden wants to talk about but can't, and then this thing he doesn't want to talk about, his age, but kind of has to.
sentences.zh: 所以，里德，你刚才向我解释了所有拜登想谈却不能谈的事情，然后是这件他不想谈、但又不得不谈的事情，也就是他的年龄。

sentences.en: And that's a pretty tough needle to thread.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当难把握的平衡。

sentences.en: How is Biden going to handle this?
sentences.zh: 拜登将如何处理这个问题？

sentences.en: What's his campaign actually going to focus on?
sentences.zh: 他的竞选团队实际上将专注于什么？

sentences.en: Well, the biggest issue for Democrats in this moment is abortion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，民主党人目前面临的最大问题是堕胎权。

sentences.en: It is the issue that energizes more Democrats to vote than any other issue.
sentences.zh: 这是比任何其他议题都能激发更多民主党人投票的议题。

sentences.en: And it is the issue that turns more Republicans and swing voters to vote for Democrats than any other issue.
sentences.zh: 也是比任何其他议题都能让更多共和党人和摇摆选民转而投票给民主党人的议题。

sentences.en: They have seen the success of running on abortion from the midterms to the Wisconsin Supreme Court election in April to the governor's race in Kentucky in November and a referendum on abortion rights in Ohio that won 57% of the vote in a deeply red state.
sentences.zh: 他们已经看到了主打堕胎权议题所带来的成功，从中期选举到4月份的威斯康星州最高法院选举，再到11月份肯塔基州的州长竞选，以及俄亥俄州关于堕胎权的公投，该公投在一个深红州赢得了57%的选票。

sentences.en: And so one of the big challenges for the Biden campaign, frankly, and for Democrats running for Congress and the Senate,
sentences.zh: 因此，坦率地说，对于拜登竞选团队以及竞选国会众参两院的民主党人来说，面临的一大挑战

sentences.en: will be to make it clear to voters that abortion rights are on the ballot next November.
sentences.zh: 将是向选民明确阐明，堕胎权将在今年11月的选票上进行表决。

sentences.en: And so we have started to see this from candidates for the House and Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经开始从众议院和参议院的候选人身上看到这一点了。

sentences.en: It's a little more complicated for Joe Biden because he has a long and tortured history with abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 对乔·拜登来说这要复杂一些，因为他在堕胎权问题上有着一段漫长而纠结的历史。

sentences.en: He doesn't say the word abortion with much frequency when he says it at all.
sentences.zh: 他并不经常说出“堕胎”这个词，如果说的话也是如此。

sentences.en: Being an 80-year-old Catholic, it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 作为一名80岁的天主教徒，这很艰难。

sentences.en: Being an 81-year-old Catholic who, for much of his career in politics, was not a staunch proponent of abortion rights up until his last presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 作为一个81岁的天主教徒，在他的大部分政治生涯中，他并不是堕胎权的坚定支持者，直到他上一次竞选总统时才改变。

sentences.en: And so one thing that we have seen from his supporters when they offer him unsolicited advice is that he needs to say the word abortion more often.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们从他的支持者那里看到的一点是，当他们主动提出建议时，他们认为他需要更频繁地说出“堕胎”这个词。

sentences.en: They see the power of this issue in their constituencies, in their states,
sentences.zh: 他们看到了这个议题在他们的选区、在他们的州所具有的力量，

sentences.en: and they are pressing the White House in public and private to have Biden say the word abortion and make his campaign a referendum on abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 他们正在公开和私下向白宫施压，要求拜登说出“堕胎”这个词，并把他的竞选变成一场关于堕胎权的公投。

sentences.en: Okay, so his campaign wants him to say the word abortion more, wants abortion to be kind of a part of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他的竞选团队希望他更多地说出“堕胎”这个词，希望堕胎成为他竞选活动的一部分。

sentences.en: But what would he actually say about it?
sentences.zh: 但他实际上会对此说些什么呢？

sentences.en: Because, you know, I get how Democrats at the state level would want to talk about it, you know, because abortion is playing out at the state level right now.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，我理解为什么州级层面的民主党人会想讨论这个，你知道的，因为堕胎权现在正处于州级层面的博弈中。

sentences.en: But what's the point of someone running for president talking about it?
sentences.zh: 但一个竞选总统的人谈论这个有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's not being decided at a federal level.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，这并非由联邦层面决定。

sentences.en: Well, not yet, but it could be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前还没有，但可能会是。

sentences.en: And one thing that we have heard from Democrats is that they would like to pass federal legislation codifying the right to an abortion,
sentences.zh: 我们从民主党人那里听到的一点是，他们希望通过联邦立法将堕胎权编纂成法，

sentences.en: whether that's some sort of Roe standard that they could pass into law at a federal level.
sentences.zh: 无论那是以某种罗诉韦德案的标准，让他们能够在联邦层面通过法律。

sentences.en: But at the very least, what they have is scaring people about what Republicans would do if they had the White House in control of both chambers of Congress.
sentences.zh: 但至少，他们所做的是通过制造恐惧，让人们担心如果共和党人入主白宫并控制国会两院会做些什么。

sentences.en: Because that seems pretty clear, at least what they have said they would do.
sentences.zh: 因为这看起来相当清楚，至少从他们声称自己会做的事情来看是这样的。

sentences.en: Some of that has played out in the Republican presidential debates.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分已经在共和党总统辩论中上演了。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham has talked about a 15-week ban.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆谈到了15周的禁令。

sentences.en: The new House speaker has talked about a total ban on abortion.
sentences.zh: 新任众议院议长谈到了全面禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: And so if Trump were to win and have control of Congress, it's not unreasonable to think that they would enact an abortion ban.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果特朗普获胜并控制了国会，认为他们会颁布堕胎禁令并不是不合理的推测。

sentences.en: And so that is what the Biden campaign and Biden himself have to run againSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是拜登竞选团队和拜登本人必须与之对抗的目标。

sentences.en: And it's not really difficult to imagine that Trump will give them more fodder on that front.
sentences.zh: 而且不难想象，特朗普会在这方面为他们提供更多素材。

sentences.en: You know, he is not terribly disciplined in how he talks about a lot of these issues.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在谈论许多这类议题时并没有什么纪律性。

sentences.en: And he is the guy who appointed three of the Supreme Court justices who overturned the right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 而且他正是那个任命了推翻堕胎权的的三位最高法院大法官的人。

sentences.en: So there's this quite interesting new political reality we have now with abortion where it's no longer a liability.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们现在有了一种非常有趣的关于堕胎的新政治现实，它不再是一个累赘。

sentences.en: It's actually an asset.
sentences.zh: 它实际上成了一笔资产。

sentences.en: And it's been helping Democrats a lot up and down the ballot and could potentially even help President Biden in his campaign.
sentences.zh: 它一直在各个层面上大大帮助了民主党人，甚至可能在总统大选中帮助拜登。

sentences.en: But you also mentioned Trump here and this contrast with Trump.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才也在这里提到了特朗普以及与特朗普的对比。

sentences.en: Talk to me a little bit about that, Reid.
sentences.zh: 跟我多聊聊这个，里德。

sentences.en: How is that playing into Biden's campaign?
sentences.zh: 这在拜登的竞选中起到什么作用？

sentences.en: Well, the thing that the Biden campaign believes it needs to do is convince voters that this election is not a referendum on whether you like Joe Biden,
sentences.zh: 嗯，拜登竞选团队认为他们需要做的是让选民确信，这次选举不是关于你是否喜欢乔·拜登的公投，

sentences.en: but that it's a choice between Joe Biden and a return to Donald Trump and everything that went along with it.
sentences.zh: 而是乔·拜登与重返唐纳德·特朗普时代及其带来的一切之间的一场抉择。

sentences.en: And the theory is what there?
sentences.zh: 那里的核心逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: The theory is that voters may be dissatisfied with Joe Biden and they may not be in love with Joe Biden and they may not like that he's 81 years old.
sentences.zh: 核心逻辑是，选民可能对乔·拜登感到不满，他们可能并不深爱乔·拜登，他们也可能不喜欢他已经81岁高龄。

sentences.en: But they elected him in the first place because they really didn't like Donald Trump and they didn't like the idea of having a chaotic presence in the White House that was in their lives on a daily basis in their Facebook feeds and on the news.
sentences.zh: 但他们当初选他，是因为他们真的很讨厌唐纳德·特朗普，他们不喜欢白宫里有一个混乱的存在，这个存在每天都出现在他们的生活中、他们的Facebook动态里以及新闻里。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Trump, if you remember when Trump was in the White House, he was the topic of conversations that, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，特朗普，如果你还记得特朗普在白宫的时候，他一直是人们谈论的话题，你知道的，

sentences.en: literally games and PTA meetings and like it was just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 简直是游戏和家长教师联谊会讨论的焦点，无处不在。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: It's like it's like it's like the metaphor was there's a horse in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 就像那个比喻说的那样，医院里跑进来一匹马。

sentences.en: Where's it going to be next?
sentences.zh: 接下来它要去哪儿？

sentences.en: The horse is in the elevator.
sentences.zh: 马进电梯了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: It's like it was everybody was kind of off guard with this idea that there was chaos erupting literally everywhere at every time.
sentences.zh: 就像是每个人都对这种随时随地爆发混乱的局面毫无防备。

sentences.en: And what Biden was was a promise to not be chaotic,
sentences.zh: 而拜登代表的是一个不会带来混乱的承诺，

sentences.en: that you wouldn't you could live your life and go through many days at a time without thinking about Joe Biden and without thinking about the president.
sentences.zh: 那就是你可以过好自己的生活，连续很多天都不用去想乔·拜登，也不用去想总统是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So so they're betting that this chaotic presence is going to come roaring back onto the political scene and suddenly everybody's going to remember who this guy is.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以他们押注这种混乱的存在将卷土重来，重新杀回政治舞台，突然之间每个人都会想起这家伙是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But their problem is that Trump is much easier to ignore now than he was when he was in the White House.
sentences.zh: 但他们的问题在于，现在要忽视特朗普比他在白宫时容易多了。

sentences.en: The cable networks don't carry his rallies live.
sentences.zh: 有线电视网不再直播他的集会。

sentences.en: He's not active on the major social media platforMs.
sentences.zh: 他在主流社交媒体平台上并不活跃。

sentences.en: You know, news of him is a little more siloed than it was before.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，关于他的新闻比以前更加孤立和碎片化了。

sentences.en: And so part of the challenge for the Biden campaign, frankly, is putting Trump back in those people's lives.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，拜登竞选团队面临的部分挑战，就是把特朗普重新拉回这些人的生活中。

sentences.en: Donald Trump often says we're now, quote, we're now a failing nation.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普经常说我们现在，引述原话，“我们现在是一个正在衰落的国家。”

sentences.en: And so we've seen a conscious shift from the Biden campaign and even from Biden himself in turning their campaign into a not Trump apparatus.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到拜登竞选团队甚至拜登本人都有了一个有意识的转变，将他们的竞选转变为一个反特朗普的机器。

sentences.en: You know, we always believe diversity is our strength as a nation.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们始终相信多元化是作为国家的优势。

sentences.en: I don't believe, as the president, former president said again yesterday, that immigrants are polluting, polluting our blood.
sentences.zh: 作为总统，我不相信正如前总统昨天再次所说的那样，移民正在污染、污染我们的血液。

sentences.en: Because their bet is that if people can hear Trump saying things that are outrageous, but not so out of character for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的押注是，如果人们能听到特朗普说出那些离谱的话，但又非常符合唐纳德·特朗普的性格。

sentences.en: Trump says the Constitution gave him, quote, the right to do whatever he wants as president, end of quote.
sentences.zh: 特朗普说宪法赋予了他，引述原话，“作为总统想做什么就做什么的权利，引述结束。”

sentences.en: It will remind people of the chaos they did not like when he was the president.
sentences.zh: 这会提醒人们想起当他是总统时他们所讨厌的混乱。

sentences.en: Just remember how the pandemic hit black businesses especially hard, how my predecessor on his watch,
sentences.zh: 只要想想大流行是如何对黑人企业造成尤其沉重的打击，我的前任在任期间，

sentences.en: women and minority owned small businesses found themselves last in line accessing emergency relief.
sentences.zh: 妇女和少数族裔拥有的小企业在获得紧急救济时发现自己排在最后。

sentences.en: And scare people into voting for Joe Biden and against Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 并以此吓唬选民投票给乔·拜登并反对唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And that's pretty interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 这相当有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: They're actually trying to give more oxygen to this guy that the oxygen was taken away from after January 6th and he lost the election.
sentences.zh: 他们在1月6日之后和输掉选举之后，实际上在试图给这个被抽走了氧气的家伙提供更多的氧气。

sentences.en: I mean, trying to put him smack dab back into the middle of the political landscape is, you know, an interesting strategy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，试图把他硬生生地重新塞回政治景观的正中央，你知道的，这是一个有趣的策略。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, they have concluded that every day that the news is about Donald Trump is a good day for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们得出的结论是，新闻围绕着唐纳德·特朗普的每一天，对乔·拜登来说都是好日子。

sentences.en: So, Reid, it really seems like a lot of Biden's campaign strategy is just kind of wait and see.
sentences.zh: 所以，里德，这看起来真的很像拜登的很多竞选策略就是“走一步看一步”。

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't feel like he's really in the driver's seat steering the bus.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，感觉他并没有真正坐在驾驶座上掌控方向。

sentences.en: He's just sort of waiting for things to break his way, like he's playing defense, not offense.
sentences.zh: 他只是在等待事情朝着对有利的方向发展，就像他在打防守，而不是进攻。

sentences.en: And it's kind of puzzling because, you know, he's an incumbent with a good economy.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人费解，因为，你知道的，他是一个拥有良好经济数据的在任总统。

sentences.en: He's managed to get some major legislation passed and he's running against a potential convicted felon.
sentences.zh: 他成功通过了一些重大的立法，而且他的竞选对手是一个潜在的被定罪的重罪犯。

sentences.en: But he's still performing very poorly.
sentences.zh: 但他表现仍然很糟糕。

sentences.en: Has the Biden campaign been dealt a particularly tough hand or is it just uniquely bad at messaging?
sentences.zh: 拜登的竞选团队是不是拿到了一手特别烂的牌，还是说他们的信息传达能力实在太差了？

sentences.en: Well, Joe Biden himself is not great at messaging, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，乔·拜登本人并不擅长传达政治信息，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's not Barack Obama, right?
sentences.zh: 他不是巴拉克·奥巴马，对吧？

sentences.en: He, you know, he doesn't draw huge crowds.
sentences.zh: 他，你知道的，他吸引不了庞大的集会人群。

sentences.en: He doesn't draw the sort of intense loyalty of Bernie Sanders even.
sentences.zh: 他甚至无法吸引伯尼·桑德斯那种强烈程度的忠诚度。

sentences.en: Even when he when he was running for president in 2020, like there weren't crowds of like many thousands of people coming out to see Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 即使他在2020年竞选总统时，也没有成千上万的人山人海出来看乔·拜登。

sentences.en: He was a consensus candidate because people thought he could beat Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他是一个共识候选人，因为人们认为他能击败唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: The Trump voters I was interviewing a lot of the time were always talking about that.
sentences.zh: 我经常采访的特朗普选民总是在谈论这个。

sentences.en: Look at the stadiuMs.
sentences.zh: 看看体育场。

sentences.en: No one's there.
sentences.zh: 根本没人去。

sentences.en: No one shows up for him.
sentences.zh: 没人为他出现。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But a vote from somebody who is super excited about a candidate counts the same as a vote from somebody who is kind of meh but thinks he's better than the other guy.
sentences.zh: 但一个对候选人超级狂热的人投的一票，和那种觉得“也就那样”、但认为他比另一个人更好的选民投的一票，分量是一样的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Biden campaign needs a lot of those latter type of people to come out and vote for him and to stop Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 拜登的竞选团队需要大量后面那种类型的民众出来投票支持他，以阻止唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And I think what you're going to see over the course of the year is an intense amount of messaging to tell people that the stakes of the election are to stop Donald Trump and all that that entails.
sentences.zh: 我认为你接下来在这一年里会看到的是，大量的宣传信息告诉人们，这次选举的利害关系在于阻止唐纳德·特朗普以及这所带来的一切。

sentences.en: And so things like abortion and health care and democracy and all of these other issues will get folded under that umbrella of stopping Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 因此，诸如堕胎、医疗保健、民主以及所有这些其他议题，都会被归入阻止唐纳德·特朗普这一大伞之下。

sentences.en: And that is what they're going to push and try to impress upon people that that's the choice in this election is between a return to Donald Trump and the chaos that he brought and the relative stability,
sentences.zh: 这就是他们将要推动并试图给人们留下深刻印象的，这次选举的选择是在重返唐纳德·特朗普及其带来的混乱，与相对的稳定之间做出抉择，

sentences.en: even if people are deeply unhappy about it, that they have with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们对此深感不满，但他们与乔·拜登在一起时确实享有这种相对稳定。

sentences.en: Reid, thank you.
sentences.zh: 里德，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the president of Harvard University, Claudine Gay, announced her resignation after a series of accusations of plagiarism in her scholarly work.
sentences.zh: 周二，哈佛大学校长克劳丁·盖伊在她的学术著作被指控存在一系列抄袭行为后宣布辞职。

sentences.en: Her tenure, which began in July, was the shortest of any president in the history of the university.
sentences.zh: 她的任期始于7月，是该校历史上所有校长中任期最短的。

sentences.en: Support for her new presidency eroded in December after Gay gave what critics saw as lawyerly evasive answers at a congressional hearing about anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 12月，在盖伊在关于反犹太主义的国会听证会上给出批评者眼中“如律师般闪烁其词、迴避问题”的回答后，人们对她新任校长职务的支持开始瓦解。

sentences.en: On college campuses, Gay was Harvard's first black president and the second woman to lead the institution.
sentences.zh: 在大学校园里，盖伊是哈佛的第一位黑人校长，也是领导该机构的第二位女性。

sentences.en: And at least 55 people were killed in a powerful earthquake that struck Western Japan on New Year's Day.
sentences.zh: 元旦当天，日本西部发生强烈地震，造成至少55人死亡。

sentences.en: The quake, which registered 7.6 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, left widespread destruction.
sentences.zh: 这次地震在日本地震烈度表上达到7.6级，造成了广泛的破坏。

sentences.en: Nearly 60,000 people fled their homes.
sentences.zh: 近6万人逃离家园。

sentences.en: And on Tuesday, the authorities were continuing to search for people under the rubble.
sentences.zh: 周二，当局继续在废墟下搜寻人员。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Mary Wilson and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由玛丽·威尔逊和埃里克·克鲁普克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor with help from Rachel Quester and Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒剪辑，雷切尔·奎斯特和佩奇·考维特提供了协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marian Lozano, Rowan Nemisto, Diane Wong, and Will Reed.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛扎诺、罗万·内米斯托、黛安·王和威尔·里德的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由 Alyssa Moxley 负责工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 的 Jim Brunberg 和 Ben Landsberg 创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦里西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为节日期间的待客做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的实用技巧。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到断片才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或食物不耐受的情况吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
